newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Army sergeant pleads not guilty to assault.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Army sergeant pleads not guilty to assault.

text.p: A U.S. Army sergeant pleaded not guilty Monday to all charges brought against him in the latest court martial linked to accusations of sexual misconduct at this military training base.
Staff Sgt. George Blackley pleaded not guilty to charges that included failure to obey a general regulation, indecent assault, maltreatment and showing disrespect to a fellow noncomissioned officer.
Prosecutors said that among other things Blackley fondled a woman recruit's breasts at least twice. The recruit was testifying Monday.

Blackley was the third sergeant to be court-martialed here as a result of an ongoing investigation into trainees' complaints of abuse, assault and harassment. The Army says the investigation is not related to the rape and sexual harassment probe underway at the Aberdeen Proving Ground in Maryland.
In the last month, two other sergeants at the base were sentenced to confinement and demoted after each pleaded guilty to charges ranging from assault and battery to misconduct.

One, Loren Taylor, admitted he had consensual sex with recruits. Another sergeant, Anthony Fore, said he touched several trainees' breasts. Army regulations forbid all sexual relationships between commanders and subordinates.
